strongest_angle: A canonical and literary comparison of Arthur Conan Doyle's Sherlock Holmes and Maurice Leblanc's Arsène Lupin, examining their contrasting methods, residences, and iconic fictional encounters.

key_facts.fact: Arthur Conan Doyle first introduced Sherlock Holmes in his 1887 novel A Study in Scarlet, establishing his residence in London.
Brian Clark presented a comparative analysis of Sherlock Holmes and Arsène Lupin to the John Openshaw Society in Houston, Texas, USA on 21st April 2024.
Maurice Leblanc's character Arsène Lupin is characterized as a gentleman burglar residing in Paris, contrasting with Holmes's base in London.
David Drake from Université Paris VIII documented that Arsène Lupin triumphs by solving the mystery of the Château of Thibermesnil while relieving Holmes of his watch.
